content.value_statement: Bioinformatics users need reliable examples for reading and writing genomic data formats. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through pysam workflows for alignments, variants, sequences, coverage, and file conversion.
actual_capabilities: Provides examples for opening, querying, and writing SAM, BAM, and CRAM alignment files.
Explains VCF and BCF reading, filtering, genotype access, and variant writing with pysam.
Shows FASTA and FASTQ sequence extraction, quality filtering, and format conversion patterns.
Documents tabix-indexed BED, GTF, GFF, and VCF region queries.
Provides integrated workflow examples for coverage analysis, variant validation, and sequence context extraction.
Covers coordinate systems, indexing requirements, file modes, and performance considerations.
limitations: Requires pysam and valid genomic files in the user environment.
Many random access workflows require matching index files such as BAI, CRAI, FAI, TBI, or CSI.
Examples may need adaptation for large datasets, sample naming, and local file paths.
Does not provide biological interpretation or clinical validation of results.

use_cases.title: Build alignment quality checks
use_cases.description: Create workflows that count mapped reads, duplicates, coverage, and basic BAM statistics.

use_cases.title: Filter and summarize variants
use_cases.description: Read VCF or BCF files, inspect INFO fields, filter genotypes, and export concise variant summaries.

use_cases.title: Prepare pipeline sequence inputs
use_cases.description: Extract reference regions, process FASTQ reads, and convert sequence data for downstream tools.

prompt_templates.title: Open a genomic file
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use of pysam file classes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pysam skill to show how I should open my local BAM, VCF, FASTA, or FASTQ file and inspect its main records.

prompt_templates.title: Query a genomic region
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pysam skill to help me fetch records from a genomic region and explain which coordinate system applies.

prompt_templates.title: Create a filtering workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pysam skill to design a workflow that filters reads or variants by quality and writes a new local output file.

prompt_templates.title: Combine multiple data types
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pysam skill to plan an integrated BAM, VCF, and FASTA workflow for coverage-aware variant validation.

output_examples.input: Ask for a plan to calculate coverage over selected genome intervals.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step coverage workflow with file prerequisites, indexing notes, region handling, and summary metrics to report.

output_examples.input: Ask how to extract sequences around variants in a VCF file.
output_examples.output: An explanation of 1-based and 0-based coordinate conversion, FASTA indexing requirements, and expected FASTA-style output records.

output_examples.input: Ask how to filter FASTQ reads by quality.
output_examples.output: A practical workflow that streams reads, calculates mean quality, writes retained reads, and avoids loading the full file into memory.

best_practices: Confirm whether each operation expects 0-based numeric coordinates or 1-based region strings.
Create and verify required index files before using region-based queries.
Use explicit input and output paths, and avoid overwriting original analysis files.
anti_patterns: Mixing coordinate conventions without conversion checks.
Loading entire large BAM, FASTQ, or VCF files into memory when streaming is possible.
Running format conversion or indexing commands on original files without backup outputs.

faq.question: What file types does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers SAM, BAM, CRAM, VCF, BCF, FASTA, FASTQ, BED, GTF, GFF, and tabix-indexed files.

faq.question: Does this skill install pysam?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user must install pysam in the active Python environment.

faq.question: Why do many examples mention index files?
faq.answer: Pysam needs indexes for many random access operations on BAM, CRAM, FASTA, compressed VCF, BCF, and tabix files.

faq.question: Can it help with coordinate conversion?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when pysam uses 0-based numeric coordinates and when region strings use samtools or VCF conventions.

faq.question: Can this skill interpret clinical significance?
faq.answer: No. It helps process genomic files, but biological or clinical interpretation requires validated domain resources.

faq.question: Is it suitable for large sequencing files?
faq.answer: Yes, when workflows use streaming, indexed access, batching, and memory-aware processing patterns.
